fields.overview: Fuzuli is a city in southwestern Azerbaijan, capital of Fuzuli District, located in the Karabakh economic region near the foothills of the Lesser Caucasus. Named after the celebrated 16th-century Azerbaijani/Ottoman poet Muhammad Fuzuli, the city was occupied by Armenian forces from 1993 to 2020 and left largely in ruins. Since its recapture by Azerbaijan in October 2020, Fuzuli has become a centerpiece of the government's Karabakh reconstruction program, including a new international airport and planned "smart city" infrastructure.
fields.famous_landmarks: Fuzuli International Airport, Garghabazar Caravanserai, Haji Giyaseddin Mosque, Azykh Cave (a paleoanthropological site of global scientific interest located in the Fuzuli district), Ongoing reconstruction landmarks tied to Azerbaijan's "Great Return" resettlement program (new housing developments, public buildings).
